doc.name: A — whisky catalogue, editorial shadow play, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: single-malt bottle and rocks glass
Category: whisky
Shot programme: editorial shadow play
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a whisky catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the extreme wide set in an editorial shadow play treatment.

SUBJECT. A single-malt bottle and rocks glass. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Wide frame with the product small in a large, deliberately empty set. Shoot on a 45mm tilt-shift with the plane tipped at f/1.4, framing for a shallow out-of-focus foreground element occluding the lower third.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with flickering firelight as the only motivated source. Stage the product on or against raw board-formed concrete, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

CAMERA. Product on a stepped plinth arrangement at two heights. Shoot on a 50mm anamorphic with 2x squeeze at f/2, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hair light and background separation light with the key pulled two stops down. Stage the product on or against unglazed stoneware, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.
